findings.title: Gratitude changes the receiver, not the possessor
findings.claim: The focus's al-Ghani and al-Hamid can be heard through 31:12's gratitude and ingratitude alternatives: gratitude benefits its own subject, while the divine predicates remain after both responses. The same nonreciprocal relation returns in 14:8's collective disbelief and 27:40's gratitude test.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are al-Ghani at 31:26:9:2 and al-Hamid at 31:26:10:2. In 31:12 the HFT trace places gratitude, self-benefit, and ingratitude before the same paired predicates; 14:8 repeats Ghani-Hamid after even collective disbelief, and 27:40 puts self-benefiting gratitude before Ghani. These independent contexts make the focus pair read as worth and sufficiency that human response does not supply or diminish.
findings.reader_payoff: The closing attributes remain ordinary sufficiency and praiseworthiness, while also making visible that gratitude or refusal changes the human side of the relation rather than repairing or reducing God.
findings.containment: This is a contextual relation, not a claim that either focus adjective lexically means 'unaffected by gratitude.' The HFT record explicitly leaves open that 31:12's pair may simply close its warning; the 14:8 and 27:40 connections supply exact Arabic but no target morphology, so their role remains surface-contextual.

In 31:10 the supplied text joins the upper source to falling water and resulting vegetation. The HFT's split-root mapping activates a mark on the upper carrier, fertile ground as its receiving surface, and al-Hamid as discoverable through experience; their contact changes the cosmic merism from a pair of regions into a surface bearing evidence.
findings.reader_payoff: The familiar heavens-earth pair also carries a surprising image of provision becoming visible on the lower surface and thus open to recognition.
findings.containment: This is the HFT's explicitly form-distant split mapping from the heaven root to marking, retained as a latent graphic analogy and not as the lexical meaning of the focus noun. The ordinary location and praiseworthiness readings remain intact. The context morphology is not supplied, and the live alternative is that 31:10 simply presents creation signs without a material-writing image.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers and branch records are present, and 31:10 Arabic plus exact HFT sky-word indices are supplied; the form-distant split mapping and context-side lexical identities are legacy_unbound.

findings.title: Ownership and its closing pair recur together
findings.claim: The focus's total ownership followed by al-Ghani and al-Hamid recurs almost intact in 22:64. That wider repetition lets the final pair be heard as a recurring interpretive closure to cosmic possession rather than a loosely appended compliment.
findings.mechanism: The focus words for heavens, earth, al-Ghani, and al-Hamid carry the three-part relation. The exact Arabic supplied for 22:64 again states what is in the heavens and earth as God's, then names Him al-Ghani al-Hamid. This independent occurrence joins the same terms and changes the focus's final pair into part of a repeated formula.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how the attributes interpret the ownership clause as a connected whole.
findings.containment: One supplied parallel establishes recurrence, not a full cross-Quran system or a claim that 31:26 derives from 22:64. The target morphology is not supplied; the relation is surface-level.

epistemic.reason: The connection record supplies exact target Arabic and an explicit formulation-level relation, but no target morphology or lexical analysis.

findings.title: Al-Ghani against human need
findings.claim: The focus's al-Ghani also resonates as a relational contrast: 35:15 calls people needy toward God immediately before naming Him al-Ghani al-Hamid. Cosmic ownership can therefore be read alongside the dependence of those within the owned world.
findings.mechanism: The focus adjective at 31:26:9:2 carries independence from need. In the separate 35:15 surface, the people are named as needy toward God and the same al-Ghani title follows. That explicit contrast returns through the focus word and changes the title from an abstract property into an asymmetry between dependent creatures and their independent possessor.
findings.reader_payoff: The ownership statement becomes relational: those within the cosmic domain need its owner, while the owner does not need them.
findings.containment: This connection supplies a contextual contrast only. It does not claim that 31:26 itself states that every entity in the heavens and earth is needy, or that al-Ghani loses its ordinary meaning. The 35:15 target morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The connection record gives exact Arabic and an explicit human-need contrast, but no target morphology or lexical analysis.
